evidence.repairDesign:
# Receipt identity correction found by the frozen PostgreSQL candidate

The six terminal completion cases fail their persisted round-trip assertion. SQL commits
the compound accounting, but the loaded StrategyResultReceipt loses ExecutionRunId.

Root cause: ProcessPersistenceMappers.SerializeDiagnostics writes the legacy array
when HostCapabilityEvidence is null. ExecutionRunId is stored on each diagnostic entry.
An empty diagnostic array therefore cannot retain the supplied execution identity.
This is not an attestation requirement: ResolvePersistedExecutionRunId permits no
attestation and rejects contradictory supplied attestations. Preserve that rule.

Minimal correction, after reconciling and retaining the frozen run:

- Keep the exact legacy array for no host evidence when execution identity is absent
  or at least one diagnostic carries it.
- For an empty diagnostic list with an execution identity, write the existing version-1
  object, which already has ResultExecutionRunId and nullable HostCapabilityEvidence.
- Preserve the decoder and all identity/attestation consistency checks. No schema or
  database migration, receipt version, inferred attestation or authorization change.
- Run the existing result acceptance guard against the persisted state already loaded
  by the unit of work before returning, still inside its fenced transaction. This adds
  no query and prevents a future mapper or storage discrepancy from committing a
  terminal result whose original execution identity was lost.
- Add independent mapper tests for empty diagnostics and null host evidence, original
  array compatibility, exact execution lookup, and malformed/conflicting identity.
- Inject loss of the serialized identity after SaveChanges and require complete
  rollback of runtime, result, child and budget in the real PostgreSQL transaction.
- Repeat the complete affected candidate and existing ProcessPersistenceStoreTests;
  direct-build Persistence and refresh standard Unit/Integration outputs. Repeat full
  static enforcement and the architecture diff for the changed mapper.

The initial candidate remains frozen during its execution. No source correction has
been applied yet. Initial expected count is 282, including 216 passing Unit cases.
evidence.optionalJoinRepairDesign:
# Optional decision rows: exact repair boundary

The repaired 367-case candidate exposed four failures among the 77 existing
ProcessPersistenceStoreTests. EF InMemory evaluates a non-nullable decision-head
join key after the optional head join and throws "Nullable object must have a value".
All seven independent mapper cases and all 23 PostgreSQL completion cases pass.
The current source and binaries stay frozen until execution, reconciliation and retention.

Correct the single result-query owner after retaining this candidate:

- Explicitly lift optional head keys to nullable Guid/int before joining generations.
- Explicitly handle an absent budget before joining its parent scope.
- Guard correlated allocation/child predicates against absent budget/head rows.
- Preserve the same indexed query and projection; add no early probe round-trip,
  provider-specific branch, InMemory bypass or swallowed exception.
- Add PostgreSQL legacy result regressions with neither budget nor decision head, both
  with and without an execution ID: the selected query returns null and the actual unit
  of work persists/replays its result.

Invalidated proof: all 77 ProcessPersistenceStoreTests, the 23 completion tests plus
the two legacy cases, and the nine registered result tests. Expected successor: 111 cases.
The unchanged 223 remaining pure/dispatcher/recovery/mapping cases do not use this EF
query; the 21 budget cases and 14 original-reader cases have no added strategy result.
Retain those 258 passing behaviors only if the complete source diff is exactly the
reviewed query and new integration-test delta, with documentation changes identified.
Repeat direct Persistence build, dependent standard outputs, full static enforcement,
architecture query review, exact discovery, source/runtime identity and resource checks.
No test-only workaround or broad-suite pass is claimed.
